record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: For a conducting sequence beta in {0,1}*, let u shuffled with itself using beta denote the interleaving determined by beta. Which square-free words u can be shuffled with themselves to obtain another square-free word?

evidence.quote: Which square-free words u can be shuffled to obtain a square-free word u  beta u?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the set of finite words over A. A word w ∈ A* is square-free if it contains no non-empty factor of the form xx, i.e., there are no factorizations w = pxxq with x ≠ ε.

Given a word u = a_1 a_2 ⋯ a_n ∈ A* and a binary "conducting sequence" β = b_1 b_2 ⋯ b_{2n} ∈ {0,1}^{2n} containing exactly n zeros and n ones, define the shuffle of u with itself directed by β, denoted u ⧢_β u, to be the unique word w_1 w_2 ⋯ w_{2n} obtained as follows: read β from left to right and let i (resp. j) be the running count of 0's (resp. 1's) seen so far; if b_k = 0 set w_k = a_i (the i-th letter of the first copy of u), and if b_k = 1 set w_k = a_j (the j-th letter of the second copy of u). Equivalently, u ⧢_β u is an interleaving of two copies of u where β specifies, position by position, from which copy the next letter is drawn.

Characterize the set of square-free words u ∈ A* for which there exists a conducting sequence β ∈ {0,1}^{2|u|} (with equal numbers of 0's and 1's) such that the shuffle u ⧢_β u is again a square-free word. The same question may be posed for infinite square-free words u, with β ∈ {0,1}^ω having infinitely many 0's and 1's.
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of (infinite) square-free self-shuffling words was established by Müller, Puzynina, and Rao (Electronic J. Combinatorics, 2015), answering a question of Harju in the affirmative. Subsequent work (e.g., Currie–Saari; Harju–Müller) studies square-free shuffles further, and recent work on shuffled-square-free words (Guégan–Ochem and successors, 2022–2023) addresses related avoidance problems. However, a complete characterization of which square-free words u admit a conducting sequence β making u ⧢_β u square-free does not appear to be fully established; the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On Shuffling of Infinite Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: They affirmatively demonstrate that square-free self-shuffling words do exist, answering Harju's question.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of square-free self-shuffling words is established, but a full characterization is not.

status_evidence.title: Square-free shuffles of words - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.claim: Continuing line of work on square-free shuffles, indicating problem is actively studied rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.title: On shuffled-square-free words
status_evidence.snippet: There exist arbitrarily long shuffled-square-free words on alphabets with 6 or more letters.
status_evidence.claim: Related avoidance problem partially resolved; characterization question remains.
